Platform limitations

  • limitation
    The in-process Responses API contact is synchronous and tool-free; API-only output is never promoted into repository or review authority.
    source
    docs/provider-setup.html, Grok primary Cursor-family profile
  • limitation
    The Grok Build CLI is a native-host capability. A containerized Director cannot use the Windows executable or a host worktree path without an authenticated host runner.
    source
    docs/provider-setup.html, Grok primary Cursor-family profile
  • limitation
    Readiness fails closed unless the endpoint is exactly the official xAI API base, tools stay disabled, every bound is valid, and any elevated authority has a nonempty explicit CLI worktree map.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/config.py:grok_primary_readiness
  • limitation
    Draft-PR work requires an isolated grok/* worktree and may create one draft PR but may not merge it.
    source
    docs/provider-setup.html, Grok primary Cursor-family profile
  • limitation
    Grok Bot is named by the charter as a distinct contact but has no adapter, transport enum value, or configuration variable in this repository.
    source
    docs/team-operating-charter.html; src/director_orchestrator/interactions.py:ProviderTransport
  • limitation
    Owner-reported account context: lower-capacity paid service; API billing and quotas must be verified separately.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/config.py:provider_strategy

Communication

relay_rule
provider_messages_relay_through_director
direct_provider_to_provider_channels_exist
false
notes
  • Grok reaches Claude, Cursor, OpenAI, and every other lane only through Director-authored packets, declared dependency outcomes, review handoffs, and moderated debate turns.
  • Grok never posts to the Slack thread; the Director relays a concise assignment-correlated summary.
  • Grok Bot, if ever implemented, would be a Director-to-Grok contact, not a peer channel.

This profile does not change

  • committee voting weights or the immutable denominator
  • runtime permissions or allowlists
  • provider credentials
  • deployments or service state
  • Slack behaviour
  • deterministic policy in src/director_orchestrator/policy.py
